topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture on the complement system and sets expectations for the session.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core architecture of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the basic organization, naming conventions, and central functional role of component C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the three biochemical recognition routes that initiate complement and converge to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the downstream immune mechanisms employed by activated complement to clear pathogens and promote inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory proteins and checkpoint mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the disease presentations and clinical pathologies resulting from deficiencies in individual complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It explores the evolutionary survival strategies pathogens employ to subvert complement defenses, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
